MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Keep active. NSAIDs (regular) for flare. Physiotherapy referral. Avoid imaging in non-specific low back pain. Reassure if no neurology. NICE NG59.

options.label: Mild to Moderate (Sensory only / Nocturnal symptoms)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Specialist Care):
1. Primary: Targeted corticosteroid injection (e.g. 20-40mg Methylprednisolone) into carpal tunnel. Highly effective for symptom relief.
2. Splintage: Mandatory neutral-angle nocturnal wrist splints for 8 weeks.
3. Neuro-monitoring: Repeat NCS in 3-6 months if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Severe (Motor deficit / Thenar atrophy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Surgical Care):
1. Gold Standard: Open or endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release (CTR).
2. Urgency: Required within 4-8 weeks to prevent irreversible axotomy/atrophy.
3. NCS Findings: Expect prolonged distal motor latency (DML > 4.5ms) and absent/reduced amplitudes.

options.label: Initial Screening
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
History: Sleep, stress, diet, drugs. Bloods: FBC, Ferritin, U&E, TFT, HbA1c, Vit D, Bone, LFT, Coeliac screen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected ME/CFS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Persistent fatigue >3 months. Check NICE NG206 for diagnostic criteria. Do not offer LET or GET. Focus on energy management (pacing).

options.label: Diagnosis (BMS Toolkit)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Clinical: >45y with vasomotor symptoms and irregular periods (perimenopause) or no period ≥1y (menopause).
2. FSH: Only if <40 (premature) or 40-45 with atypia. Do not use FSH if on hormonal contraception.
3. Discussion: Review benefits vs risks (low risk in <60y/within 10y of onset). NICE NG23 / BMS.

options.label: HRT: Systemic Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BMS Gold Standard):
1. Choice: Transdermal (Gel/Patch) preferred if BMI >30, Migraine, or high VTE risk.
2. Progesterone: Micronised Progesterone (Utrogestan) 100mg nocte (continuous) or 200mg (cyclical days 15-26) is the metabolic gold standard.
3. Mirena IUS: Excellent for endometrial protection and contraception.
4. Testosterone: Trial if low libido despite adequate oestrogen (specialist initiation). BMS.

options.label: Atrophic Vaginitis (GSM)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topicals: Vaginal Oestriol (Ovestin) or Estradiol (Vagifem/Imvaggis). Use daily for 2w then twice weekly indefinitely.
2. Note: Safe to use long-term even if systemic HRT contraindicated (discuss with oncology if breast cancer). NICE NG23.

options.label: Combined Hormonal (CHC) - UKMEC
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Screening: BP, BMI, Migraine with aura (MEC 4), Smoking >35y (MEC 4), VTE history (MEC 4).
2. Missed Pill: 24h+ late? Check FSRH missed pill tool. Usually, 1 pill missed = take ASAP and no extra care. 2+ pills = extra care for 7 days.
3. Breakout Bleeding: Exclude STI. If persist, increase oestrogen dose or change progestogen type.

options.label: Long-Acting (LARC)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Mirena/Levosert: Now licensed for 8 years for contraception (if fitted age ≥25).
2. Nexplanon: Effective for 3 years. Inform about irregular bleeding pattern.
3. Copper IUD: Non-hormonal. Gold standard for emergency contraception (within 5 days).

options.label: Emergency Contraception
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (FSRH):
1. Copper IUD: Most effective (MEC 1 in majority). Up to 5 days after UPSI.
2. Ulipristal (ellaOne): Up to 5 days (120h). Avoid progestogens for 5 days after ellaOne.
3. Levonorgestrel: Up to 3 days (72h). Double dose (3mg) if BMI >30 or on enzyme-inducers.

options.label: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding (HMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG88):
1. 1st-line: Mirena IUS (if acceptable).
2. 2nd-line: Tranexamic Acid (1g tds during period) +/- Mefenamic Acid (500mg tds).
3. Hormonal: COCP or High-dose Progestogens (Medroxyprogesterone).
4. Investigation: Pelvic US if uterus large/fibroids, or fail medical tx.

options.label: PCOS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BMS/RCOG):
1. Diagnosis: Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: Anovulation, Hyperandrogenism, Polycystic ovaries).
2. Protection: Prevent endometrial hyperplasia via IUS or COCP (ensure ≥4 bleeds/year).
3. Metabolic: Screen for T2DM (HbA1c) and CVD risk. Metformin if insulin resistant. NICE NG28, CKS PCOS.

options.label: Endometriosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG73):
1. Trial: 3-6 months COCP or POP. NSAIDs for pain.
2. Imaging: Pelvic US (specialist endometriosis scan if deep involvement suspected).
3. Referral: To BSGE Endometriosis centre if severe/refractory or bowel/bladder involvement.

options.label: Post-Menopausal Bleeding (PMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG/NICE):
1. Triage: Any vaginal bleeding in a post-menopausal woman not on HRT, or unexpected bleeding on HRT.
2. Action: Urgent 2WW Referral for Ultrasound +/- Hysteroscopy/Biopsy.
3. Cut-off: Endometrial thickness > 4mm in PMB requires biopsy. NICE NG12.

options.label: Freezing Stage (Painful / Inflammatory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Grade):
1. Primary Intervention: US-guided Intra-articular Corticosteroid Injection (40mg Triamcinolone). Superior to PT in early stage.
2. Analgesia: Scheduled NSAIDs (e.g. Naproxen 500mg bd with PPI) + Paracetamol/Codeine as rescue.
3. Physiotherapy: Gentle active-assisted ROM within pain-free limits. Avoid aggressive stretching in inflammatory phase.
4. Education: Natural history (12-24 month duration). NICE CKS / BESS Guidelines.

options.label: Frozen Stage (Stiff / Fibrotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Grade):
1. Hydrodilatation: Consider high-volume image-guided distension (Injecting 20-30ml saline + steroid) to disrupt capsular adhesions.
2. Physiotherapy: Home Exercise Programme (HEP) focusing on external rotation and abduction. 4-5 times daily.
3. Monitoring: Review for secondary rotator cuff disuse atrophy. NICE CKS / BESS Guidelines.

options.label: Refractory / Severe Functional Impairment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Grade):
1. Surgical Referral: Orthopaedic review for Manipulation Under Anaesthesia (MUA) or Arthroscopic Capsular Release (ACR).
2. Indication: Failure of 6 months conservative management with significant impact on sleep/QoL.
3. Post-Op: Mandatory immediate intensive PT to maintain surgical gains.

options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

templates.evidence: RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye, Blepharitis, Dry eye, Glaucoma; NICE NG81 (glaucoma), NG28 (diabetic retinopathy).

options.label: Dry eyes / Blepharitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dry eye: Preservative-free artificial tears (hypromellose, carmellose); lid hygiene; review screen use. Blepharitis: warm compresses, lid massage, lid hygiene. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Stye / Chalazion / Subconjunctival haemorrhage
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stye (hordeolum): warm compresses; chloramphenicol if infected. Chalazion: warm compresses; refer if large or persistent. Subconjunctival haemorrhage: reassure; check BP if recurrent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Viral/allergic: cool compresses, lubricants. Bacterial: chloramphenicol 0.5% 2-hourly 2 days then qds. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day (RCOphth). NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Glaucoma (chronic open-angle)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Ophthalmology-led. Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. latanoprost) first-line. Monitor IOP and visual fields. Urgent referral if acute angle-closure suspected (pain, nausea, hard globe). NICE NG81; RCOphth.

options.label: When to refer (RCOphth)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: corneal ulcer/keratitis, acute uveitis, acute angle-closure, scleritis, chemical/trauma, sudden vision loss, post-surgery pain. 2WW: referable diabetic retinopathy. Routine: chronic glaucoma, dry eye, chalazion. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE NG12, NG28, NG81.

options.label: No Red Flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Proceed to conservative or medical management. NICE NG12.

options.label: URGENT 2WW Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dysphagia (any age).
2. Unintentional weight loss + dyspepsia (≥55y).
3. Upper abdominal mass. NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 1: Lifestyle & Antacids
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Weight loss; stop smoking; avoid meal-to-bed gap (<3h).
2. Raise head of bed. Avoid triggers (coffee, spice, alcohol). NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 2: Full-dose PPI
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Omeprazole 20mg or Lansoprazole 30mg OD for 1 month.
2. Review: If symptoms controlled, reduce to 'as needed' low dose. NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 3: H. pylori Testing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Test if dyspepsia persistent despite PPI (ensure off PPI for 2 weeks before test).
2. If Urea Breath Test / Stool Antigen positive: Eradication therapy. NICE NG12.

options.label: Benign Lumps (Indications for GP Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Symptomatic (pain, inflammation, interference with function). 
2. Lipomas: Usually only if >5cm or rapidly growing (refer for US first to exclude sarcoma).
3. Sebaceous Cysts: Excise if recurrently infected (wait for infection to settle first).
4. Exclusions: Cosmetic removal is generally not routinely publicly funded.

options.label: Red Flags (Refer to 2WW / Plastic Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Changing Naevi: Refer to 2WW Dermatology.
2. Irregular, fixed, or hard masses: Urgent referral.
3. Note: Never excise a lesion where malignancy is suspected in primary care minor surgery clinic.

options.label: Common Injections (Standard Pack)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Drugs: Triamcinolone (Kenalog) 40mg or Depo-Medrone 40mg + 1% Lidocaine.
2. Areas: Shoulder (Subacromial), Knee (Intra-articular), Trigger Finger (Tendon sheath), Carpal Tunnel.
3. Post-op: 48 hours of joint rest. Warn about 'steroid flare' (pain increase for 24-48h).

options.label: Cautions & Consent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diabetics: Warn about blood sugar rise (may last 1-2 weeks).
2. Anticoagulation: Safe if INR in therapeutic range (<3.0).
3. Infection: Absolutely contraindicated if skin infection over site or suspected septic arthritis.

options.label: Suture Removal Timings
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Face: 3-5 days (prevents scarring).
2. Scalp: 7-10 days.
3. Trunk / Arms: 10-14 days.
4. Legs / Extensor Surfaces: 14 days.
5. Note: Remove alternate sutures first if wound tension is high.

options.label: Wound Dressing Selection
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dry/Sutured: Film (Tegaderm) or simple island dressing.
2. Sloughy: Hydrogel (Intrasite).
3. Highly Exudative: Foam (Allevyn) or Alginate.
4. Infected: Honey (Medihoney) or Silver dressings.

options.label: Anticipatory Meds (The 'Big 4')
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pain/SOB: Morphine Sulfate 2.5mg - 5mg SC prn.
2. Secretions: Hyoscine Butylbromide 20mg SC prn.
3. Agitation: Midazolam 2.5mg - 5mg SC prn.
4. Nausea: Levomepromazine 6.25mg SC prn.
5. Note: Ensure Just-in-Case box is in house and District Nurses are informed.

options.label: Verification of Death
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm identity.
2. 5 mins observation: No respiratory effort, no palpable pulse, fixed dilated pupils.
3. Documentation: Record time of death and clinical findings clearly.

options.label: Med3 (Fit Notes)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First 7 days: Patient self-certifies (Employer cannot demand Med3).
2. >7 days: Clinician issues Med3 based on clinical assessment.
3. Note: Focus on what patient 'can' do (phased return, amended duties) where possible.

options.label: Safeguarding (Adult/Child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify: Physical, emotional, sexual abuse, or neglect (including self-neglect in adults).
2. Action: Discuss with Designated Lead. Urgent referral to MASH (Children) or Adult Social Care if risk is immediate.
3. Documentation: Use factual, objective language. Do not promise confidentiality if disclosure is required for safety.

options.label: Continuity & QOF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Disease: Annual review (QOF) including bloods and symptom score.
2. Polypharmacy: Holistic medication review (SMR) with clinical pharmacist for patients on >10 meds.

options.label: Specialist Triage Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Dual-Track Care**: Simultaneous stabilization of medical risk (Refeeding/Cardiovascular) and intensive specialized psychotherapy.
2. **Biological**: Focus on electrolyte balance (K, PO4, Mg) and cardiac rhythm. Nutritional rehabilitation is the primary goal.
3. **Psychological**: Addressing the 'cognitive anorexic core' and body image distortion using specialized models (MANTRA/CBT-ED).
4. **Systemic**: Multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement is mandatory (Psychiatrist, Dietitian, Specialist Nurse).

options.label: Life-Threatening Markers
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cardiovascular: HR <40 bpm, SBP <90 mmHg, QTc prolongation.
2. Metabolic: K+ <3.0, Phosphate <0.5 (Refeeding risk), Glucose <3.0.
3. Physical: Temp <35.5°C, BMI <13. 
4. Action: Emergency admission to medical ward + specialist ED liaison.

options.label: Anorexia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: AN-top (Anorexia Nervosa Focused Psychotherapy), MANTRA (Maudsley Anorexia Nervosa Treatment for Adults), or CBT-ED.

options.label: Bulimia (Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: Bulimia-focused CBT (CBT-BN) or IPT.

options.label: Prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Risk assess (e.g. Waterlow/Braden). Repositioning; pressure-relieving surfaces; skin care; nutrition.
2. Offload pressure; manage moisture, friction, shear. NICE NG179, CKS.

options.label: Treatment & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Wound care per category (1–4). Treat infection; debridement if needed. Urgent referral if category 3–4, deteriorating, or suspected deep tissue injury. NICE NG179.

options.label: Assessment & intervention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Multifactorial assessment: medication review (sedatives, hypotensives), vision, footwear, home hazards, strength/balance. Treat osteoporosis if fracture risk.
2. Exercise (strength and balance); vitamin D; address orthostatic hypotension. NICE CG161, NG231.

options.label: Principles
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Minimise initiation; shortest duration; regular review. Taper when stopping (benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, opioids, gabapentinoids).
2. Shared decision-making; support for withdrawal. Do not stop abruptly. NICE NG215, CKS.

options.label: Consultant Population Health Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Prevention**: Shifting from reactive care to proactive wellbeing management.
2. **Universal Factors**: Sleep, Nutrition, Connection, and Sense of Agency.
3. **Social Prescribing**: Utilizing non-medical community assets to address medical drivers.

options.label: Actions & Resources
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **5 Ways to Wellbeing**: Connect, Be Active, Take Notice, Keep Learning, Give.
2. **Sleep Hygiene**: Regular times, avoid screens, caffeine limit.
3. **Support**: Signpost to local 'Talking Therapies' (IAPT) and peer-support networks.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

options.label: Consultant Approach to Somatisation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Philosophy**: Shift from 'Is it physical OR mental?' to 'How is the nervous system communicating distress?'.
2. **Validation**: Acknowledge symptoms are REAL (not 'it's all in your head').
3. **Mechanism**: Dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system or 'top-down' sensory processing errors (FND).
4. **Goal**: Manage symptoms and improve function rather than 'eliminating' the sensation.

options.label: Functional Neurological Disorder (FND)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Based on *positive signs* (e.g. Hoover's sign for leg weakness), not just exclusion.
2. Therapy: Specialized Physiotherapy (re-training movement) + CBT focused on symptom retraining.
3. Meds: Low-dose TCAs (Amitriptyline) for co-morbid pain/sleep.

options.label: Somatisation / MUS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Schedule: Regular 15-min appointments (regardless of symptom flare) to reduce 'crisis-driven' care.
2. Education: Use metaphors (e.g. 'Software vs Hardware' problem).
3. Meds: SSRIs if significant co-morbid anxiety/depression.

options.label: Consultant Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Priority**: Reduce fatalities (Overdose prevention).
2. **Assessment**: Frequency, route (IV risk), cost, and criminal justice involvement.
3. **Dual Diagnosis**: High correlation with trauma (PTSD) and EUPD. Treat co-morbidities simultaneously.

options.label: Opioid Dependence (Heroin/Methadone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. OAT: Opioid Agonist Treatment (Methadone or Buprenorphine) is the standard of care.
2. Safety: Provide Naloxone kits for home use. Screening for Hep C and HIV.

options.label: Cannabis/Cocaine
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Psychosocial (CBT, Motivational Interviewing, Contingency Management).
2. Meds: No licensed maintenance pharmacotherapy. Symptom management only.

options.label: The 5 Core Principles (MCA 2005)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Presume Capacity**: Unless proven otherwise.
2. **Support to Decide**: All practicable steps taken to help.
3. **Unwise Decisions**: Do not equal lack of capacity.
4. **Best Interests**: Decisions for those lacking capacity must be in their BI.
5. **Least Restrictive**: Choose the option that restricts rights the least.

options.label: 2-Stage Functional Test
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Diagnostic Stage**: Is there an impairment of or disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain?
2. **Functional Stage**: Can the patient:
   - **Understand** the information?
   - **Retain** the information?
   - **Use or Weigh** the information?
   - **Communicate** the decision?

options.label: Consultant LD Ethos
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Diagnostic Overshadowing**: Warning—don't attribute physical symptoms (e.g. pain) to the disability itself.
2. **STOMP**: Stopping Over-Medication of People with a learning disability. Avoid long-term antipsychotics for 'behaviour' unless treating a mental illness.
3. **Communication**: Use 'Easy Read' materials and Hospital Passports.

options.label: Assessment & Action
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First: Exclude pain, constipation, or environmental stressors (sensory overload).
2. Positive Behaviour Support (PBS): 1st-line intervention. Focus on identifying the 'message' behind the behaviour.

options.label: B12 Deficiency - Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-dietary (e.g. Pernicious Anaemia): Hydroxocobalamin 1mg IM every other day for 2 weeks (loading), then 1mg IM every 3 months for life.
2. Dietary: Oral cyanocobalamin 50-150mcg daily between meals, or two 1mg injections per year.
3. Monitoring: Reticulocyte count at 7-10 days; Hb/MCV at 8 weeks.
4. Review: Exclude co-existing Iron/Folate deficiency if response sub-optimal. NICE CKS.

options.label: Deficiency (<30 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Loading: 300,000 IU total over 6-10 weeks (e.g. 20,000 IU twice weekly for 7 weeks or 50,000 IU weekly for 6 weeks).
2. Maintenance: 800-2000 IU daily (or 20,000-40,000 IU monthly) lifelong if risk factors persist.
3. Safety: Avoid loading if primary hyperparathyroidism or renal stones suspected. ROS Guidelines.

options.label: Insufficiency (30-50 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Strategy: Advise dietary sources (oily fish, eggs) and safe sun exposure.
2. Supplement: 800-1000 IU daily as maintenance; loading not routinely required unless symptomatic or high-risk of progression. NICE CKS.

options.label: Oral Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Ferrous Fumarate 210mg (or Sulfate 200mg) once daily or every other day (to reduce GI side effects per recent evidence).
2. Counseling: Take on empty stomach; avoid tea/coffee/antacids within 2h.
3. Monitoring: Check Hb in 2-4 weeks. Continue for 3 months after Hb normalizes to replete stores. BSG Guidelines.

options.label: IV Iron Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Persistent intolerance to oral iron, profound deficiency with symptomatic anaemia, or malabsorption (e.g. IBD/Gastric bypass).
2. Action: Arrange Ferric Carboxymaltose (Ferinject) or Iron Isomaltoside (Monofer) infusion via local daycare unit.

options.label: Initiation: Levothyroxine
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: 1.6 mcg/kg/day (typically 50-100mcg) if young/healthy. Start 25mcg if elderly or history of IHD.
2. Counseling: Take 30-60 mins before breakfast/caffeine; separate from Calcium/Iron by 4h.
3. Review: Repeat TSH in 6-8 weeks. Adjust dose by 12.5-25mcg until euthyroid. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected Microbial Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IMMEDIATE: Emergency Same-Day Ophthalmology referral (A&E eye clinic).
2. First Aid: Stop contact lens wear immediately; do not patch the eye.
3. Note: High risk of permanent vision loss/perforation within 24-48h if untreated. Moorfields Guidelines.

options.label: Cardiorenal-Metabolic Plan
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACEi/ARB: Titrate to max tolerated dose if ACR >3mg/mmol (DM) or >30mg/mmol (non-DM).
2. SGLT2i: Add (e.g. Dapagliflozin 10mg) if eGFR >25 and ACR >22.3 mg/mmol to reduce progression risk.
3. BP Target: Aim for <140/90 (or <130/80 if ACR >70).
4. Statins: Offer Atorvastatin 20mg for primary prevention of CVD. NICE NG203.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bulk-forming laxatives; topical GTN or diltiazem. Avoid constipation. Refer if chronic or failed medical. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Alpha-blocker (tamsulosin); 5-alpha reductase inhibitor if large prostate. Rule out retention. NICE NG97, CKS.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CFS or other tool; medication review; advance care planning. Target reversible factors. NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat; stop ACEi/ARB/MRA/spironolactone if severe. Consider calcium resonium. Refer if K+ >6 or ECG changes. NICE NG203, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antiperspirant (aluminium chloride); glycopyrronium if focal. Exclude hyperthyroid. Refer if refractory. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Heat exhaustion: cool, rehydrate, rest. Heatstroke: 999; cool rapidly; IV fluids. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Report to coroner if cause unknown, violent/unusual, in custody, or notifiable. Follow local procedure. NICE CKS.

options.label: Standard Skin Care Plan
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Skincare: Use soap substitutes (emollients) for washing. Avoid harsh soaps and detergents.
2. Emollients: Apply liberal amounts of emollient cream/ointment frequently to maintain skin barrier.
3. Triggers: Identify and avoid potential irritants or allergens.
4. Safety-net: Return if signs of infection (weeping, crusting, fever) or no improvement in 2 weeks. NICE CKS.
